title: Module 11 · NICU
intro: Neonatal ages and weights, 10 fold errors, NRP epinephrine and volume, routine newborn drugs, early onset sepsis, ceftriaxone hard stops, caffeine salts, heparin vials, hypoglycemia and neonatal TPN.

cases.title: Neonatal ages and weights
cases.stem: A baby born at 30 weeks is now 14 days old. Birth weight 1.3 kg, today 1.25 kg.

options.t: 32 weeks (GA 30 + 2 weeks PNA)
30 weeks (GA alone at birth)
options.why: GA stays fixed; PMA moves forward.

options.t: 2 weeks (postnatal age only)
options.why: PNA is chronologic age, not PMA.

options.t: 34 weeks (GA + 4 weeks PNA)

steps.q: Which reference do you use to dose this baby?

options.t: Neofax or Lexicomp Pediatric, per unit charts
Adult Lexicomp, scaled down by weight
Pediatric doses for a 1 year old by weight
options.why: Infant intervals do not fit preterm neonates.

options.t: Harriet Lane only, without unit charts
options.why: Use the unit's chosen reference and charts.

steps.q: Why does the weight on the order matter so much?

options.t: A decimal slip is a 10 fold error
options.why: Tiny weights; weight also changes in the first week.

options.t: Neonatal weights rarely change early
options.why: They drop the first week, then rise.

options.t: Doses get rounded to whole mL anyway
Weight only matters for fluid orders

cases.pearl: **PMA = GA + PNA. Neonatal reference only. Check the weight every time.**

sources.t: St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

cases.title: The 10 fold error
cases.stem: Order: morphine 0.5 mg IV every 4 hours for a 1.2 kg baby. Usual neonatal IV dosing is about 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg per dose (check Neofax or Lexicomp).

options.t: 0.42 mg/kg: about 4 to 8x the usual range
options.why: And exactly 10x 0.05 mg: a classic decimal slip.

options.t: 0.042 mg/kg: within the usual range
options.why: Decimal error in the check itself.

options.t: 0.6 mg/kg: about 6 to 12x the usual range
options.why: Multiplied by weight instead of dividing.

options.t: 0.1 mg/kg: the top of the usual range
Always a leading zero (0.05 mg); never trailing (5.0)
Check mg/kg/dose vs mg/kg/day on every order
Use a trailing zero to show precision (5.0 mg)
Round all doses to whole numbers
options.why: Neonatal doses are fractions of a mg.

options.t: Write "u" for units to save space

cases.pearl: **Neonates: calculate mg/kg on every dose. Leading zero, no trailing zero.**

sources.t: St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

cases.title: Delivery room epinephrine
cases.stem: A 3 kg newborn, heart rate below 60 despite 30 seconds of effective ventilation and compressions. UVC placed.

steps.q: What is the priority before any drug?

options.t: Effective ventilation
options.why: NRP: most neonatal arrests are respiratory.

options.t: Epinephrine before ventilation
Sodium bicarbonate 2 mEq/kg
Atropine 0.02 mg/kg
0.02 mg/kg IV: 0.06 mg (0.6 mL of 0.1 mg/mL)
0.1 mg/kg IV: 0.3 mg (3 mL of 0.1 mg/mL)
options.why: 0.1 mg/kg is the endotracheal dose; IV is 0.01 to 0.03.

options.t: 0.01 mg/kg IV: 0.03 mg (0.03 mL of 1 mg/mL)
options.why: Right range but wrong concentration; use 0.1 mg/mL.

options.t: 1 mg IV: 10 mL of 0.1 mg/mL
NS 10 mL/kg (30 mL) over 5 to 10 min
NS 20 mL/kg (60 mL) as rapid IV push
options.why: The pediatric shock bolus, not NRP.

options.t: D10W 2 mL/kg (6 mL) as a bolus
Albumin 25% 10 mL/kg over 1 hour

cases.pearl: **NRP: ventilate first. Epi 0.02 mg/kg IV (0.1 mg/mL), 0.1 mg/kg ETT. NS 10 mL/kg.**

sources.t: AHA/AAP 2025 Neonatal Resuscitation Guidelines (AHA CPR and ECC 2025)
Vali et al. NRP epinephrine dosing ranges (PMC)

workup.calc: 0.02 mg/kg x 3 kg = 0.06 mg = **0.6 mL** of 0.1 mg/mL IV; ETT would be 0.1 x 3 = 0.3 mg = 3 mL. Saline 10 mL/kg = 30 mL.

cases.title: Routine newborn medications
cases.stem: A healthy term newborn. Mother is HBsAg positive.

options.t: Vitamin K 0.5 to 1 mg IM once
Erythromycin 0.5% eye ointment, both eyes
Hep B vaccine + HBIG within 12 hours
Hep B vaccine alone, HBIG at 1 month
Vitamin K 0.5 to 1 mg by mouth

cases.pearl: **Every newborn: vitamin K, eye ointment, hep B vaccine. HBsAg+ mom: add HBIG within 12 h.**

sources.t: AAP Red Book (current edition): neonatal sepsis, HSV and newborn prophylaxis

cases.title: Early onset sepsis
cases.stem: Term baby, mother had intraamniotic infection. Baby is tachypneic. Cultures drawn.

options.t: Ampicillin + gentamicin
Ceftriaxone + gentamicin
options.why: No Listeria coverage; ceftriaxone risks in neonates.

options.t: Vancomycin + gentamicin
options.why: Not the empiric early onset sepsis regimen; no MRSA risk here.

options.t: Ampicillin + azithromycin

steps.q: Why ampicillin and not a cephalosporin alone?

options.t: Cephalosporins never cover Listeria
Ampicillin covers E. coli more reliably
options.why: E. coli is often ampicillin resistant; that is why gentamicin is added.

options.t: Cephalosporins do not cover GBS
Ampicillin penetrates CSF better

steps.q: How is gentamicin dosed in neonates?

options.t: By GA/PMA and PNA on the unit chart
options.why: A term neonate is often about 4 mg/kg every 24 hours; preterm every 36 to 48 hours.

options.t: Hartford nomogram, 7 mg/kg every 24 h
2.5 mg/kg every 8 h for every neonate
options.why: Older traditional dosing; not chart based.

options.t: 4 mg/kg every 12 h for every neonate

cases.pearl: **EOS: ampicillin + gentamicin by the unit chart.**

sources.t: AAP Red Book (current edition): neonatal sepsis, HSV and newborn prophylaxis
St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

cases.title: Ceftriaxone and calcium in a neonate
cases.stem: An order for ceftriaxone in a 10 day old on TPN with calcium. Bilirubin is elevated.

options.t: No ceftriaxone with IV calcium in neonates
Ceftriaxone displaces bilirubin from albumin
Ceftriaxone needs a gentamicin partner here
Ceftriaxone must be given IM only
Nothing; it is fine at 10 days old

steps.q: Which alternative cephalosporins are used for neonatal meningitis in the US now?

options.t: Cefepime or ceftazidime with ampicillin
options.why: Cefotaxime is no longer marketed in the US.

options.t: Cefotaxime with ampicillin
options.why: No longer available in the US.

options.t: Ceftriaxone with a separate line
options.why: Still contraindicated with any IV calcium in neonates.

options.t: Cefazolin with ampicillin

cases.pearl: **Neonate + ceftriaxone: no IV calcium, no jaundice. Use cefepime or ceftazidime.**

sources.t: Kemper AR, et al. AAP clinical practice guideline: hyperbilirubinemia in newborns 35 weeks or more. Pediatrics 2022;150:e2022058859
St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

cases.title: Caffeine for apnea
cases.stem: Apnea of prematurity, 1.1 kg. Order: caffeine citrate 22 mg IV load, then 5.5 mg daily.

options.t: Yes: 20 mg/kg load, 5 mg/kg daily (citrate)
No: load should be 10 mg/kg citrate
options.why: 10 mg/kg is a base load (= 20 citrate).

options.t: No: maintenance should be 20 mg/kg daily
No: maintenance should be every 8 hours

steps.q: The order says "caffeine base." What changes?

options.t: Citrate 2 mg = base 1 mg; base order doubles it
Citrate 1 mg = base 2 mg; base order halves it
Citrate and base are equal by weight
Base is only an oral form; same dose

cases.pearl: **Caffeine citrate 20 load, 5 to 10 daily. 2 mg citrate = 1 mg base.**

sources.t: St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

workup.calc: 1.1 kg: load 20 mg/kg = 22 mg; maintenance 5 mg/kg = 5.5 mg daily (caffeine citrate).

cases.title: Heparin in the NICU
cases.stem: A neonatal line flush order reads "heparin 10 units/mL." The technician picks a vial from the shelf.

options.t: Look alike vials (10 vs 10,000 units/mL)
Heparin flushes bind calcium in TPN
Heparin 10 units/mL needs dilution
Heparin should never be used in NICU
Concentration, preservative free, volume
options.why: Count flush volume in total fluids.

options.t: Only the drug name and the expiration
Only the lot number
Only that the color of the cap matches

cases.pearl: **NICU heparin: read the concentration every time. Preservative free.**

sources.t: St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

cases.title: Neonatal hypoglycemia
cases.stem: A 3.2 kg newborn with symptomatic hypoglycemia.

options.t: D10W 2 mL/kg (6.4 mL), then infusion
D25W 2 mL/kg (6.4 mL), then infusion
D50W 1 mL/kg (3.2 mL) by IV push
options.why: Adult concentration; injures veins and causes rebound.

options.t: D10W 20 mL/kg (64 mL) as one bolus
options.why: Ten times; that is a fluid bolus volume.

cases.pearl: **Neonatal low sugar: D10W 2 mL/kg, then infusion. Never D50.**

sources.t: St. Mary's NICU dosing reference (Neofax or Lexicomp), gentamicin chart and drip concentrations (verify locally)

workup.calc: D10W 2 mL/kg x 3.2 kg = **6.4 mL** (640 mg dextrose = 200 mg/kg).

cases.title: Neonatal TPN
cases.stem: A 900 g preterm infant needs high calcium and phosphate in TPN.

steps.q: How do you reduce precipitation risk?

options.t: Solubility curve; phosphate early, calcium last
Add calcium and phosphate first, together
Raise the pH by adding bicarbonate
Switch to calcium chloride for solubility
options.why: Chloride is less soluble with phosphate.

options.t: An independent double check, every bag
One pharmacist, if experienced
Only the compounding technician
Only when the TPN has a dose change

cases.pearl: **Neonatal TPN: solubility curve, phosphate early, calcium last, cysteine, double check.**
